name: Nazareth, his own country
charge: Being offended at him; seeking to cast him down the hill
summary: In the synagogue where he had been brought up he read Isaiah and said the scripture was fulfilled that day. They marvelled, then asked if this was not the carpenter's son, then were filled with wrath and led him to the brow of the hill. He did no mighty work there, and passed through the midst of them.
offense: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary? And they were offended at him. When he reminded them that Elijah was sent to a widow of Sidon and Elisha cleansed a Syrian, all they in the synagogue were filled with wrath, and rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
judgment: A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house. And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief; he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them; and he marvelled because of their unbelief. He passing through the midst of them went his way, and Nazareth kept what it had chosen: a carpenter's son and no miracles.

entries.commentary: Being full of the Holy Ghost he is led by the Spirit into the wilderness, forty days tempted of the devil, and in those days he did eat nothing. He answers with the law: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

The devil shows him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. No man can do that, which settles who was standing there. All this power will I give thee, for that is delivered unto me, and to whomsoever I will I give it. The offer is real, and the price is worship. Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. Again the answer is a commandment.

Set on a pinnacle of the temple and answered with scripture, he replies, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God. When the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season. The whole battle was fought with the word, and that is the only way it is won.

As his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read. He reads from Esaias: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor, to preach deliverance to the captives. This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.

They wonder at the gracious words, and then ask, Is not this Joseph's son? No prophet is accepted in his own country. He names the widow of Sarepta and Naaman the Syrian, and they are filled with wrath, thrust him out of the city, and lead him to the brow of the hill to cast him down headlong, but he passes through the midst of them.

In the synagogue there was a man which had a spirit of an unclean devil, and it cried out, I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God. That spirit was sitting in the house of worship, and it knew exactly who he was. Knowing who he is and doing what he says are two different things.

He rebukes the fever in Simon's wife's mother and it leaves her, and he lays his hands on every one of the sick brought to him. I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent. He went where the people were, and some received the word and some did not.

In his own country they are astonished at his wisdom and his mighty works, and then are offended at him because they know his family. A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. What was done to him is done to those teaching today: men who knew you before you repented ask who you think you are.

He could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk and healed them, and he marvelled because of their unbelief. Consider what that means. The unbelief of his own people was such that it made the son of the Most High marvel.

He sends them forth by two and two with power over unclean spirits, taking nothing for the journey but a staff. Whosoever will not receive you nor hear you, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. The word goes out whether they hear or whether they forbear, and that shaking of the dust seals the judgment.

Herod hears of him and says it is John, whom he beheaded, risen from the dead. John had told Herod plainly, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife. Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it, because those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel.

Herodias had a quarrel against John and would have killed him, but could not, for Herod feared him, knowing that he was a just man and an holy. When the oath is made, the daughter asks her mother what to ask, and is told, The head of John the Baptist. The king was exceeding sorry, but for his oath's sake he sent the executioner.

He was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things. Five loaves and two fishes feed five thousand men, and twelve baskets of fragments are taken up. He made them sit down by companies, in ranks by hundreds and by fifties. No man argued about where he was placed. The Most High is a God of order, and the eating came after the order.

He comes to them walking upon the sea, and they suppose it had been a spirit and cry out. These were fishermen; they knew what water does. They were sore amazed, for they considered not the miracle of the loaves, for their heart was hardened. Men can watch a thing done in front of them and still not take it to heart.
Wherever he entered, they laid the sick in the streets and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment, and as many as touched him were made whole.

A sower goes forth to sow. Seed falls by the way side, on stony places, among thorns, and into good ground, and only the good ground brings forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.

It is given unto the disciples to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but not unto them. Whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance; but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.

In them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias: by hearing ye shall hear and shall not understand, and seeing ye shall see and shall not perceive. They saw the works and did not perceive. The heart was made fat and the ears heavy so that they would not be converted, because judgment had to come.
Blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear. Many prophets and righteous men desired to see these things and did not see them.

The seed by the way side is the one who hears and understands not, and the wicked one catches away what was sown in his heart. The stony ground is the one who receives it with joy and has no root, and is offended when tribulation or persecution arises. That can come through family or through a job. The thorns are the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, which choke the word. The good ground hears and understands, and brings others in behind him.

An enemy sows tares among the wheat while men slept, and the householder will not have them gathered up before the harvest lest the wheat be rooted up with them. The separating is not ours to do. Both grow together until the harvest.
The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, the least of all seeds, which becomes the greatest among herbs. This work starts small and ends covering the earth.

The leaven hid in three measures of meal leavens the whole, and all these things were spoken in parables, that it might be fulfilled, I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.

Christ gives the meaning himself: the sower is the Son of man, the field is the world, the good seed are the children of the kingdom, the tares are the children of the wicked one, the enemy is the devil, the harvest is the end of the world, and the reapers are the angels. The tares are gathered and burned, and the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hid in a field, which a man finds and for joy thereof sells all that he hath and buys that field. Finding out who you are is that joy.
The merchant man, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had and bought it.

The net gathers of every kind, and the good are put into vessels and the bad cast away. The angels sever the wicked from among the just. This is not only about the other nations. Israel must keep these laws, and there will be those in these last days who are not keeping them.
Every scribe instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like a householder which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.

In his own country they are astonished and ask, Is not this the carpenter's son? They name his mother, his brethren James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and his sisters, all of them living among them. A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country and in his own house, and he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The Word is Christ, and he was there in the beginning. The Word was with God, and the Word was of God: his wisdom and his power, which is why the same sentence can say both.
All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not. What gives life is the word itself. The flesh profits nothing; the words are spirit and they are life.

There was a man sent from God, whose name was John, sent to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe. He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of it. He prepared the way. The blessing that came down on all men is traced in the scripture to one head, and rested on Jacob and was divided among the twelve tribes.

He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not. He came unto his own, and his own received him not. His own are named all through the scriptures: the people the law was appointed to, and sin is the breaking of that law.
But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.
And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.

The law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ. Grace and mercy are said in the scriptures to be with his saints, and the truth is named in the psalm as the law itself. Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

John confessed, and denied not, but confessed, I am not the Christ, nor Elias, nor that prophet. I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias. I baptize with water: but there standeth one among you, whom ye know not. Men came to that baptism confessing their sins, and a man has to be taught the law to know what he is confessing.

Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water. John says himself who this was made known to. Upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he which baptizeth with the Holy Ghost.

Two of John's disciples follow him and ask where he dwelt. He said, Come and see, and they abode with him that day. He had a place to stay. Andrew first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, and brought him to Jesus, who said, Thou shalt be called Cephas.

We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write. What was written of him was written in the law and the prophets before ever he came. Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile. Nathanael answered, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel. That is the title given him here, and it names one people. --- Topics: [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

verses.text: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.
And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,
To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.
And he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened on him.
And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
And all bare him witness, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph’s son?
And he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.
And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.
But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;
But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.
And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.
And all they in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,
And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
But he passing through the midst of them went his way,
And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him.

And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?
Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.
But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.
And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.
And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.
And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.
And when he was come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works?
Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?
And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?
And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.
And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
For neither did his brethren believe in him.
